title: Doc-Level Index Maintenance + Draft-Aware Identity (FINAL first)
repo_context: Add doc-slice inventory/diagnose/execute for semantic indexing (FINAL_SEGMENTS v0) plus draft-aware identity/hydration enabling step for EVERYTHING.

stories.title: Make EVERYTHING view draft-aware: entry_id becomes canonical draft_id (head-only v0) + tests
acceptance_criteria: EVERYTHING enumeration emits a draft-aware ref where entry_id == draft_id
draft_id format is exactly `draft:head:<dossier_id>:<transcription_id>` for the canonical head-only v0 policy
A deterministic pytest verifies the ref identity contract for at least one fixture entry
stories.notes: This is an enabling story: it preserves head-only behavior while upgrading identity vocabulary to doc-slice draft-aware IDs.

stories.title: Make transcript hydration draft-aware for head-form draft_ids (fallback to existing behavior) + tests
acceptance_criteria: Hydrating a transcript ref with draft_id `draft:head:<did>:<tid>` deterministically loads the same head content as the legacy path
Behavior remains backward compatible for refs without draft_id
A deterministic pytest validates draft-aware hydration and produces a stable content_hash
stories.notes: Keep v0 minimal: support head-form now; add resolver-based hydration for non-head draft ids in a later story if needed.

stories.title: Add doc-slice label enumeration: list_labels_for_entry(pool,dossier,entry_id) in VectorMetadataStore + tests
acceptance_criteria: VectorMetadataStore exposes list_labels_for_entry(pool_identifier, dossier_id, entry_id) -> List[int]
A deterministic pytest inserts rows for multiple entry_ids and verifies only the target entry’s labels are returned
stories.notes: This is required to support replace-all at doc-slice resolution.

stories.title: Add delete_entry_slice(pool,dossier,entry_id): tombstone all vectors for that entry slice + tests
acceptance_criteria: Persistent store exposes delete_entry_slice(pool_identifier, dossier_id, entry_id) returning counts (or equivalent)
Deletion tombstones the slice’s labels in HNSW and marks deleted in metadata so deleted labels do not return as hits
A deterministic pytest shows that after deleting one entry slice, queries no longer return that entry’s chunks while other entry chunks still appear
stories.notes: Correctness-first; compaction remains separate and explicit.

stories.title: Persist per-slice indexed state: add indexed_entry_state table + store methods + schema bump tests
acceptance_criteria: A new SQLite table exists for per-slice state keyed by (pool_identifier, dossier_id, entry_id)
Store can upsert and read indexed_signature plus identity fields (embedding_model_fingerprint, chunking_policy_id)
A deterministic pytest verifies: missing row -> None, upsert -> row exists, upsert again -> replaces deterministically
stories.notes: This enables missing/stale/healthy diagnosis at doc-slice granularity.

stories.title: Write indexed_entry_state after slice rebuild: builder stores indexed_signature and runtime identity + tests
acceptance_criteria: After indexing a single entry slice, indexed_entry_state is updated with indexed_signature == entry.content_hash
Stored identity fields (model fingerprint + chunking policy id) match the runtime identity used for indexing
A deterministic pytest validates state is written after indexing
stories.notes: Keep signatures opaque strings. Favor dependency injection so tests can use a stub embedder.

stories.title: InventoryProvider v0 for FINAL_SEGMENTS: enumerate slices and compute desired_signature (content_hash) + tests
acceptance_criteria: InventoryProvider can list desired doc slices for FINAL_SEGMENTS with (pool_identifier, dossier_id, entry_id, desired_signature)
desired_signature is derived from deterministic hydrated entry content_hash
A deterministic pytest verifies inventory output for a small fixture without network calls
stories.notes: Start with FINAL only; EVERYTHING inventory can be added in a later phase once draft-aware hydration expands.

stories.title: Diagnose v0: compare inventory desired_signature vs indexed_entry_state to classify missing/stale/healthy/unavailable + tests
acceptance_criteria: Diagnose returns slice-level statuses for FINAL_SEGMENTS: missing (no state), stale_content (signature mismatch), stale_identity (model/policy mismatch), unavailable (hydrate failure), healthy
A deterministic pytest covers at least: missing -> stale after indexing -> healthy after rebuild, and an unavailable slice returns unavailable with a reason
stories.notes: Cheap and safe: diagnose should not perform heavy rebuild work.

stories.title: Execute v0: rebuild exactly one doc slice (delete_entry_slice + rebuild + update state) + tests
acceptance_criteria: Execute performs replace-all per doc slice for FINAL_SEGMENTS: tombstone existing slice labels then rebuild and update indexed_entry_state
A deterministic pytest changes one slice’s content, verifies diagnose marks exactly that slice stale, and execute rebuilds only that slice to return healthy
Heavy work is only done in execute path (no silent rebuild in query paths)
stories.notes: Keep policy simple and deterministic; auto-light scheduling can remain a UI concern in v0.
